arxiv-2103-08432.title: Combinatorial Resultants in the Algebraic Rigidity Matroid
arxiv-2103-08432.creator: Goran Malić, Ileana Streinu
arxiv-2103-08432.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Goran Malić, Ileana Streinu. Motivated by a rigidity-theoretic perspective on the Localization Problem in 2D, we develop an algorithm for computing circuit polynomials in the algebraic rigidity matroid CM n \operatorname{CM}_{n} associated to the Cayley-Menger ideal for n n points in 2D. We introduce combinatorial resultants , a new operation on graphs that captures properties of the Sylvester resultant of two polynomials in the algebraic rigidity matroid.

arxiv-2104-12348.title: HERMES spectroscopy of normal A and Am stars 2020 HERMES spectroscopy of normal A and Am stars – References
arxiv-2104-12348.creator: Otto Trust, Edward Jurua, Peter De Cat, Santosh Joshi, Patricia Lampens
arxiv-2104-12348.description: Abstract The nominal Kepler mission provided very high-precision photometric data. Using these data, interesting phenomena such as spots, and “hump and spike” features were observed in the light curves of some normal A and metallic lined A stars (Am stars). However, the connection between such phenomena and the chemical peculiarity of the Am stars is still unclear.

arxiv-2210-05278.title: EnsembleMOT: A Step towards Ensemble Learning of Multiple Object Tracking
arxiv-2210-05278.creator: Yunhao Du, Zihang Liu, Fei Su
arxiv-2210-05278.description: Abstract Multiple Object Tracking (MOT) has rapidly progressed in recent years. Existing works tend to design a single tracking algorithm to perform both detection and association. Though ensemble learning has been exploited in many tasks, i.e, classification and object detection, it hasn’t been studied in the MOT task, which is mainly caused by its complexity and evaluation metrics.

arxiv-2402-05794.title: Phonetically rich corpus construction for a low-resourced language
arxiv-2402-05794.creator: Marcellus Amadeus, William Alberto Cruz Castañeda, Wilmer Lobato, Niasche Aquino
arxiv-2402-05794.description: Abstract Speech technologies rely on capturing a speaker’s voice variability while obtaining comprehensive language information. Textual prompts and sentence selection methods have been proposed in the literature to comprise such adequate phonetic data, referred to as a phonetically rich corpus . However, they are still insufficient for acoustic modeling, especially critical for languages with limited resources.

arxiv-2403-15754.title: Energy Efficient Design of Active STAR-RIS-Aided SWIPT Systems Thanks: Sajad Faramarzi is with the School of Electrical Engineering, Iran University of Science & \& Technology, Tehran, Iran (e-mail: sajad.faramarzi 1397 1397 @gmail.com) Hosein Zarini is with the Dept. of Computer Engineering, Sharif
arxiv-2403-15754.creator: Sajad Faramarzi, Hosein Zarini, Sepideh Javadi, Mohammad Robat Mili, Rui Zhang, Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-2403-15754.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sajad Faramarzi, Hosein Zarini, Sepideh Javadi, Mohammad Robat Mili, Rui Zhang, Fellow, IEEE. In this paper, we consider the downlink transmission of a multi-antenna base station (BS) supported by an active simultaneously transmitting and reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS) to serve single-antenna users via simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT).

arxiv-2409-02396.title: A Dynamic Resource Scheduling Algorithm Based on Traffic Prediction for Coexistence of eMBB and Random Arrival URLLC
arxiv-2409-02396.creator: Yizhou Jiang 1 2 Xiujun Zhang 2 Xiaofeng Zhong 1 3 Shidong Zhou 1 3
arxiv-2409-02396.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a joint design for the coexistence of enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB) and ultra-reliable and random low-latency communication (URLLC) with different transmission time intervals (TTI): an eMBB scheduler operating at the beginning of each eMBB TTI to decide the coding redundancy of eMBB code blocks, and a URLLC scheduler at the beginning of each mini-slot

arxiv-2410-18861.title: Provably Robust Watermarks for Open-Source Language Models
arxiv-2410-18861.creator: Miranda Christ, Sam Gunn, Tal Malkin, Mariana Raykova
arxiv-2410-18861.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Miranda Christ, Sam Gunn, Tal Malkin, Mariana Raykova. The recent explosion of high-quality language models has necessitated new methods for identifying AI-generated text. Watermarking is a leading solution and could prove to be an essential tool in the age of generative AI. Existing approaches embed watermarks at inference and crucially rely on the large language model (LLM) specification and parameters being secret, which makes them inapplicable to the open-source setting. In this work, we introduce the first watermarking scheme for open-source LLMs.

arxiv-2501-06379.title: Macroscopic properties of the XTE J1814-338 as a dark matter admixed strange star
arxiv-2501-06379.creator: Luiz L. Lopes
arxiv-2501-06379.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Luiz L. Lopes. In this letter, I discuss the macroscopic properties of the ultracompact object XTE J1814-338, whose inferred mass and radius read M M = 1.21 ± \pm 0.05 M ⊙ M_{\odot} and R = 7.0 ± \pm 0.4 km.

arxiv-2503-11584.title: Image reconstruction from an elastically distorted scan
arxiv-2503-11584.creator: Adrian Lopez, L. Mahadevan
arxiv-2503-11584.description: Abstract We consider the problem of inverting the artifacts associated with scanning a page from an open book, i.e. "xeroxing." The process typically leads to a non-uniform combination of distortion, blurring and darkening owing to the fact that the page is bound to a stiff spine that causes the sheet of paper to be bent inhomogeneously.

arxiv-2508-02103.title: Instance-Dependent Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning via Maximum Likelihood Estimation
arxiv-2508-02103.creator: Runze Zhao, Yue Yu, Ruhan Wang, Chunfeng Huang, Dongruo Zhou
arxiv-2508-02103.description: Abstract Continuous-time reinforcement learning (CTRL) provides a natural framework for sequential decision-making in dynamic environments where interactions evolve continuously over time. While CTRL has shown growing empirical success, its ability to adapt to varying levels of problem difficulty remains poorly understood.

arxiv-2512-06559.title: Tight Universal Bounds for Partially Presorted Pareto Front and Convex Hull
arxiv-2512-06559.creator: Ivor van der Hoog, Eva Rotenberg, Daniel Rutschmann
arxiv-2512-06559.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ivor van der Hoog, Eva Rotenberg, Daniel Rutschmann. TimSort is a well-established sorting algorithm whose running time depends on how sorted the input already is. Recently, Eppstein, Goodrich, Illickan, and To designed algorithms inspired by TimSort for Pareto front, planar convex hull, and two other problems. For each of these problems, they define a Range Partition Entropy; a function H H mapping lists I I that store n n points to a number between 0 0 and log ⁡ n \log n .

arxiv-2602-15317.title: Enhancing Computational Efficiency in NetLogo: Best Practices for Running Large-Scale Agent-Based Models on AWS and Cloud Infrastructures
arxiv-2602-15317.creator: Michael A. Duprey, Georgiy V. Bobashev
arxiv-2602-15317.description: Abstract The rising complexity and scale of agent-based models (ABMs) necessitate efficient computational strategies to manage the increasing demand for processing power and memory. This manuscript provides a comprehensive guide to optimizing NetLogo, a widely used platform for ABMs, for running large-scale models on Amazon Web Services (AWS) and other cloud infrastructures.

pmc-11318383.title: Integrative human atrial modelling unravels interactive protein kinase A and Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II signalling as key determinants of atrial arrhythmogenesis
pmc-11318383.creator: Haibo Ni, Stefano Morotti, Xianwei Zhang, Dobromir Dobrev, Eleonora Grandi
pmc-11318383.description: AimsAtrial fibrillation (AF), the most prevalent clinical arrhythmia, is associated with atrial remodelling manifesting as acute and chronic alterations in expression, function, and regulation of atrial electrophysiological and Ca2+-handling processes. These AF-induced modifications crosstalk and propagate across spatial scales creating a complex pathophysiological network, which renders AF resistant to existing pharmacotherapies that predominantly target transmembrane ion channels.

pmc-11506081.title: Decoding Apelin: Its Role in Metabolic Programming, Fetal Growth, and Gestational Complications
pmc-11506081.creator: Nikolaos Loukas, Dionysios Vrachnis, Nikolaos Antonakopoulos, Sofoklis Stavros, Nikolaos Machairiotis, Alexandros Fotiou, Chryssi Christodoulaki, Markos Lolos, Georgios Maroudias, Anastasios Potiris, Petros Drakakis, Nikolaos Vrachnis
pmc-11506081.description: Placental insufficiency and gestational diabetes, which are both serious pregnancy complications, are linked to altered fetal growth, whether restricted or excessive, and result in metabolic dysfunction, hypoxic/oxidative injury, and adverse perinatal outcomes. Although much research has been carried out in this field, the underlying pathogenetic mechanisms have not as yet been fully elucidated.

pmc-11728524.title: Susceptibility of Mouse Brain to MCMV Infection and Neuroinflammation During Ontogeny
pmc-11728524.creator: Fran Krstanović, Andrea Mihalić, Lucija Šakota, Berislav Lisnić, Stipan Jonjić, Ilija Brizić, Yuying Liang
pmc-11728524.description: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) rarely infects the brain following infection of adult individuals. However, the virus readily infects the brain during congenital HCMV (cHCMV) infection, frequently causing severe neurodevelopmental and neurological sequelae. Interestingly, although the incidence of cHCMV infection is 0.5–1%, the proportion of congenitally infected individuals in which the virus manages to gain access to the brain is unknown.

pmc-12460463.title: Hematological characteristics, oxidative stress, and patient-reported symptoms in Tibetan patients with chronic mountain sickness at 4500 m altitude
pmc-12460463.creator: Yang Zhong, Fengying Zhang, Qiuyue Li, Doudou Hao, Zhiyou Shi, Yuling Liu, Suying Zhu, Pasang Tsering, Yunhong Wu
pmc-12460463.description: BackgroundChronic mountain sickness (CMS), driven by chronic hypoxia, features erythrocytosis, cardiovascular impairment, and systemic oxidative stress. Current studies focus on haematological and cardiopulmonary changes, but multidimensional features like sleep disturbances, quality of life, and oxidative stress remain underexplored.MethodsThe cross-sectional study included 47 adult Tibetan residents living at 4,500 m and diagnosed with CMS using Qinghai criteria.

pmc-12540831.title: Intelligent optimization of track and field teaching using machine learning and wearable sensors
pmc-12540831.creator: Yunxia Li, LI Wang, Ziyu Wang, QI Liu, Gang Qin, Jia Zhang
pmc-12540831.description: Traditional track and field education relies heavily on subjective assessment and manual feedback systems, creating critical barriers to personalized instruction in large-scale educational settings. This study presents a novel machine learning framework for optimizing track and field teaching through intelligent analysis and personalization of instructional content.

pmc-12651797.title: Diagnostic Value of Opportunistic CT-Based Bone Density Assessment in Patients with and Without Sacral Insufficiency Fractures
pmc-12651797.creator: Julian Ramin Andresen, Guido Schröder, Thomas Haider, Hans-Christof Schober, Reimer Andresen, Paola Pisani
pmc-12651797.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: This retrospective observational cohort examined whether opportunistic CT-derived Hounsfield units (HU) of the lumbar spine and proximal femur together with serum 25-OH-vitamin D can predict sacral insufficiency fractures (SIF) and osteoporosis. No interventional procedures were performed. Methods: Consecutive suspected SIF cases over 3 years (n = 253) were assigned to SIF (n = 98) or controls without SIF or spine/hip fractures (n = 155).

pmc-12684395.title: Gene-sized DNA insertion at genomic safe harbors in human cells using a site-directed transposase
pmc-12684395.creator: James E Short, Lisa Sharek, Joshua F Meckler, Ilko Stoytchev, Christopher T Tran, Clara Errard, Brian E Hew, Brandon E Johnson, David F Waller, Shanfu Xie, Joseph J Higgins, Raymond Tabibiazar, Jesse B Owens
pmc-12684395.description: Achieving precise and efficient integration of gene-sized DNA sequences into the human genome remains a major obstacle to gene therapy. Existing approaches depend on double-strand DNA breaks, which can lead to unintended genome alterations. Many monogenic diseases arise from diverse patient-specific mutations, making individualized correction impractical and underscoring the need for universal full-gene replacement strategies.

pmc-12972085.title: Harnessing fano-like line shape resonance in a rectangular waveguide for filtering applications
pmc-12972085.creator: El-Aouni Mimoun, Ali Hennache, Ben-Ali Youssef, Essahlaoui Abdelouahed, Bria Driss, Mahmoud A Zaky, Zaky A Zaky
pmc-12972085.description: This study presents a comprehensive investigation of the transmission characteristics and filtering performance of a tailored one-dimensional rectangular waveguide structure (1D-RWS). The research employs a combined analytical–numerical approach. The system is first modeled theoretically using the Green’s function method (GFM) to elucidate the underlying physical mechanisms and then validated through rigorous finite element method (FEM) simulations.

pmc-13053226.title: Long-term prognostic comparison of surgery followed by adjuvant chemoradiotherapy versus definitive chemoradiotherapy in T4N0-3M0 esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a single-center retrospective cohort study
pmc-13053226.creator: Shiwang Wen, Hesong Wang, Xiaohan Zhao, Shuguang Li, Chunyang Song, Wenzhao Deng, Jingyuan Wen, Shuchai Zhu, Wenbin Shen
pmc-13053226.description: BackgroundThis large retrospective study aimed to compare the long-term survival outcomes of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) patients with stage T4N0-3M0 treated with surgery followed by adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (S+CRT) versus definitive chemoradiotherapy (dCRT).MethodsPatients with T4N0-3M0 ESCC who received S+CRT or dCRT at our institution between January 2011 and December 2018 were included in the study.

pmc-13236720.title: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for Bipolar Depression: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials: Stimulation magnétique transcrânienne dans les cas de dépression bipolaire : une revue systématique et une méta-analyse d’essais contrôlés à répartition aléatoire
pmc-13236720.creator: Carl Zhou, Nicholas Fabiano, Stanley Wong, Mikkel Højlund, Risa Shorr, Michel Sabé, Mattia Campana, Joshua Hyde, Valerie Brandt, Samuele Cortese, Sara Tremblay, Ram Brender, Gayatri Saraf, Lakshmi N. Yatham, Marco Solmi
pmc-13236720.description: IntroductionBipolar depression is disabling and often inadequately responsive to medication alone. The current efficacy evidence of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) for bipolar depression is conflicting. Therefore, we synthesized randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that tested the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of TMS for bipolar depression.MethodsWe searched MEDLINE/EMBASE/Cochrane/PsycINFO/gray literature (01/10/2025) for RCTs comparing any TMS protocol with sham.

pmc-13251767.title: Structural and functional characterization of human kallistatin
pmc-13251767.creator: Stephanie T.D. Pham, Kristian W. Nielsen, Jonas H. Graversen, Nanna Kristensen, Lasse B. Steffensen, Andrea R. Lundgaard, José L. Martín-Ventura, Peter Højrup, Yaseelan Palarasah
pmc-13251767.description: Kallistatin is a serine protease inhibitor (serpin) that specifically inhibits tissue kallikrein, a key enzyme involved in kinin generation and vascular homeostasis. While serpins are known to polymerize under certain conditions, the structural properties of human kallistatin—particularly its glycosylation profile, tissue distribution, and polymerization potential—remain poorly defined.

pmc-13422587.title: Evaluation of the Impact of a Mobile App (LoAD Calc) on the Calculation of Maximum Safe Doses of Local Anesthetics: Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-13422587.creator: Alexandra Stefani, Pietro Elias Fubini, Tal Sarah Beckmann, Caroline Flora Samer, Georges Louis Savoldelli, Mélanie Suppan

pmc-13607355.title: Maternal and Neonatal Outcomes in Pregnancies with PCR-Confirmed SARS-CoV-2 Infection Ending in Live Birth: A Single-Centre Turkish Cohort Benchmarked Against National Reference Data
pmc-13607355.creator: Oğuzhan Elçi, Ali Benian
pmc-13607355.description: Background/Objectives: Most evidence on SARS-CoV-2 infection in pregnancy comes from hospitalised or symptomatic cohorts sampled early in the pandemic. We described maternal and neonatal outcomes in an unselected cohort of PCR-confirmed infections ending in live birth, identified characteristics associated with neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission and with prolonged maternal hospitalisation, and benchmarked event rates against national data.

pmc-13633987.title: Endocrine and neuromodulatory regulation during prolonged maximal 6000-m rowing in male athletes
pmc-13633987.creator: Joanna Ostapiuk-Karolczuk, Anna Kasperska, Hanna Dziewiecka, Justyna Cichoń-Woźniak, Małgorzata Reysner, Wojciech Gruszka, Piotr Basta, Sabina Kaczmarczyk, Anna Skarpańska-Stejnborn
pmc-13633987.description: PurposeThe 6000-m rowing ergometer test represents a prolonged maximal effort commonly used in elite rowing; however, its physiological responses are less well characterized than those observed during the standard 2000-m race-distance format. This study aimed to examine acute endocrine and neuromodulatory responses to a maximal 6000-m rowing test in elite male rowers.
